thesisQuality.note: Arm's royalty/licensing model and broad compute IP footprint create a high-quality structural thesis, tempered by valuation and control concentration.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: FY2026 revenue grew 22.8% and earnings 14.1%; Q4 revenue grew 20% with very high gross margin.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: About $284B market cap with roughly 270x trailing and 111x forward P/E leaves little valuation margin of safety.

catalystScore.note: AI/cloud/edge adoption and continued licensing/royalty conversion provide substantial forward catalysts; next earnings is Nov. 4, 2026.

governancePower.note: Public-company reporting is current, but concentrated SoftBank ownership/control reduces minority-holder governance independence versus a widely held issuer.

alignment2036.note: CPU, GPU, NPU, system IP and compute subsystems directly address heterogeneous AI/cloud/edge compute scaling.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Licensing, royalties, CSS and software/tooling reinforce one architecture ecosystem across mobile, cloud, automotive and edge markets.

bottleneckControl.note: Arm architecture/IP is deeply embedded across semiconductor design ecosystems, creating an important compute-design control point without assuming monopoly power.

scenarioRobustness.note: Diversified end markets and an asset-light IP model support resilience across compute scenarios, though architecture shifts remain a real counterfactual.

substitutionResilience.note: Large installed software/developer ecosystem and pervasive architecture licensing create high switching friction; RISC-V remains the principal substitution threat.

supplyChainResilience.note: IP licensing is comparatively asset-light and March liquidity exceeded $3.6B, reducing direct manufacturing supply-chain exposure.

pricingPower.note: Near-98% Q4 GAAP gross margin and royalty/licensing economics demonstrate exceptional value capture, while customer bargaining power caps a perfect score.

risk1.note: Extreme valuation, concentrated control, semiconductor/customer cyclicality and open-architecture substitution can materially impair expected returns despite strong business quality.

confidence.note: Current primary 20-F/Q1 filing plus current independent market valuation support all numeric components; customer-level concentration remains explicit non-gating uncertainty.

thesis: Arm's pervasive architecture and royalty model form a durable control layer for increasingly heterogeneous AI, cloud, automotive and edge compute.
keyRisk: The current valuation prices extraordinary execution while concentrated control and RISC-V substitution constrain margin of safety.
nextCatalyst: FY2027 Q2 results expected November 4, 2026 and continued AI/cloud CSS royalty conversion.
